A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SamS research. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support reliable matching despite the revised title, added checklist, and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original preference-optimization experiments, noise tests, ablations, computational measurements, and a GPT-based dataset audit in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, robustness tests, scheduler ablations, and the dataset audit.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the reward definitions, exploitation/exploration networks, encoder, lagged updates, pretraining, and historical batch pool are unchanged. The new batch-wise terminology describes the existing procedure; no RLHF adaptation is implemented.

E1.justification: Both versions use Anthropic-HH, SHP, UltraFeedback-derived preference datasets, AlpacaEval 2, and MT-Bench, including the same noisy-label scenarios. Newly cited benchmarks and prospective RLHF/supervised-learning applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SFT, RRHF, SLiC-HF, IPO, CPO, KTO, ORPO, R-DPO, DPO, and DPO (50%), with unchanged participation under each model setting. Tables 2–3 retain the same DPO/KTO and Selective DPO comparisons.

E3.justification: The policy and reward models, dataset splits, metrics, learning rates, batch-size-64/select-32 configuration, 20% label flipping, and 2,000-sample dataset audit are unchanged. No evaluation design or previously stated setting is revised.

E4.justification: Both retain the label-noise tests, computational-cost analysis, selection-ratio ablation, exploration-network removal experiment, and GPT-audited examples. Appendix D.4 and Figure 5 test the same questions with the same evidence.

E5.justification: v4's new checklist item 7 states that all reported results average runs with 10 random seeds; v2 does not disclose this. This establishes newly reported run information, not an increase in runs. No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including Tables 1–3 and 6–8. For example, both report Mistral DPO+SamS AlpacaEval 2 LC of 33.6% and WR of 36.2%. Table 6 is relocated without changing its entries.

T1.justification: The contextual-bandit formulation, mathematical definitions, and Equations (1)–(14) are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs; the new checklist merely states the absence of theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly suggest that batch-wise selection can extend to RLHF and broader supervised learning. This modestly broadens the claimed significance beyond fixed-dataset preference optimization, while the core SamS contribution and empirical claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 newly presents applicability to RLHF and other supervised-learning paradigms as a prospective implication. Existing explanations concerning OOD responses, noise robustness, and diminishing benefits with higher-quality data in Appendix A remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Checklist item 5 newly states that complete code and running instructions are provided in supplementary materials. The existing code link, hardware disclosure, hyperparameters, and implementation details in Appendices D and F are unchanged; the PDFs do not independently establish the supplementary resources' contents.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds references and brief discussion spanning recent RLHF/reasoning work, visual tracking, image restoration, and normalization; Appendix F.2 adds citations supporting its existing encoder motivation. The positioning against active feedback collection, dueling bandits, and offline data pre-selection is retained.

P1.justification: v4 adds a conference checklist with answers and guidelines, revises the title and affiliations, and makes localized abstract, introduction, and related-work additions. The main narrative, Sections 1–7, and Appendix A–F organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: All five figures and eight tables are retained without scientific redesign. Appendix reflow moves Table 6 after the beginning of D.4 and shifts the ablation and dataset-audit displays. The checklist introduces additional list-formatted pages.

improvement.justification: The new ten-seed averaging disclosure and clearer batch-wise framing modestly improve reporting transparency. The scientific evidence remains unchanged, with no added dispersion estimates or validation of the prospective RLHF/supervised-learning extension. The checklist's unresolved Appendix ?? reference is a small editorial drawback, limiting the overall gain.
